title: English File Upper-Intermediate, File 5: second, third and mixed conditionals; wish (check against the book)

fixIt.text: If I had more time, I learn the guitar.
If she had told me, I would have help her.
fixIt.explain: Third conditional: would have + past participle.

fixIt.text: I wish I have a bigger flat.
fixIt.explain: wish + past simple for a present wish.

fixIt.text: I wish you would stop interrupt me.
fixIt.explain: stop + -ing = not do it any more.

fixIt.text: She wishes she hadn't eat so much last night.
fixIt.explain: wish + past perfect for a past regret.

fixIt.text: If only I knew the answer yesterday!
fixIt.explain: A past regret: If only + past perfect.

fixIt.text: If I were you, I'll apologise.
fixIt.explain: Advice with If I were you: I'd (would).

builder.text: If I had known, I would have helped.
alternatives: I would have helped if I had known.

builder.text: If I were you, I'd go.
alternatives: I'd go if I were you.

radio.title: A different choice
radio.text: If my father had not moved to Phnom Penh when he was young, I would probably be a farmer now, like my grandparents. Sometimes I wish I lived in the countryside, where life is slower. But if I had grown up there, I would not have gone to university, and I would not have met my husband. If only I could have both: a quiet village and a good job. My grandmother says I wish for too much.
